en: Thank you. But is your back okay?
Watchin' you hard at work made me forget all about it. I feel right as rain now. Ahaha!
That's good, I guess.
Sure...
Give my regards to the chief, too, eh? See ya!
Sorry about that. I hope I at least gave your back some more time to recover.
I guess I was so hyped up watchin' ya work that I forgot about it. I'm all better now! Ahaha!
Good for you.
Give the chief a holler for me too, okay? See ya!
You can now play the ramen minigame anytime by entering the ramen stall.
We live at the Café Portugal building over on Nagasu Boulevard. Mom and dad should be working there right now.
Portugal, huh? All right. I'll bring your dad over right away.
Excuse me. This is Café Portugal, right? Are you Haruka's father?
You've seen my daughter!? She ran off and hasn't come home!

I know. I actually saw her not too long ago. I can take you
to where she is, if you'd like.
Of course! Lead the way!
Ugh, how am I supposed to practice these questions without the answer book? I'm screwed!
If only someone could help me solve them...!
Excuse me, sir? Yes, you! You haven't seen my answer book, have you? It's one of those study guides with questions and answers from past exams. I think I dropped it somewhere!
You did what?
Oh, I'm in deep doo-doo now! Without those answers I'm as good as dead! Why does this sort of thing always happen to me!?
You're not making any sense. Calm down and explain yourself.
Okay, well, you see, I have a practice exam today. To help me prepare for actual entrance exams.
So I wanted to study up on some questions for the college I want to get into... But I lost the freaking answer book!
And if I don't know the answers, there's no point in looking at these old questions! It'd be a complete waste of time!
But you've been studying hard up until now, right? What difference will a little more right before the exam make?
It makes all the difference to me! If I don't cram before an exam, I'll panic and draw a complete blank!
I thought taking a practice test would help boost my confidence... But at this rate, the actual one will be a disaster!
I can't afford to take another year off to study if I don't pass. All my hard work would go down the drain!
Gah, what a mess! I even got up early to go buy a good luck charm to boost my literary luck... But the only thing that got boosted was my propensity for failure!
No, wait... I think I get it now!
I was carrying the answer book in my hands when I went to the shrine. I must have dropped it when I bought that charm!
That's it! I bet I'm getting punished for putting off my visit to the shrine too long!
Don't be ridiculous. It wasn't the shrine that did this to you, it was your own carelessness.
Hey, I don't need any more guilt on my shoulders right now! Are you trying to give me a mental block? I'll start forgetting all the stuff I learned!
Sounds like you've got some deeper issues to worry about than this one test, then.
What? Are you saying there's something wrong with <Italic>me</Italic>!? Well, this is just who I am!
Argh, but what am I supposed to do!? I don't have time to go back to the shrine... If only someone could help me solve these questions!
Not me. You still have some time before your test, though. I'm sure you can think of something.
You mean, use my brain? Aw crap, it's all over!
What if I helped you?
Huh? And how do you intend to do that?
Isn't it obvious? Show me the questions, and I'll tell you the answers. Then you won't need that book.
That's your plan!? You think a guy like you can just waltz in and start answering college entrance exam questions!?
Hey, don't assume things before you give me a chance. Come on, show me those questions.
Fine. I really doubt you can help, but it's not like I have any other options.
(Let's see... First up is English vocabulary.)

Question:
The spider uses a unique method of locomotion.
What does <Color:220,255,255,255>"locomotion"<Color:Default> mean in this sentence?
The answer is attack.
Really? Are you sure about that? How do you even break down the word locomotion anyway?
It's simple. Loco means crazy, and motion means movement. Put them together and you get "crazy moves," like a spider suddenly lunging at its prey.
The answer is movement.
Locomotion means movement, or the ability to move from one place to another. There's nothing else it could be.
Hey, I think you're right! It's all starting to come back to me... Yeah, that's gotta be it!
These entrance exams seem pretty easy to me.
Wow, you're actually pretty smart! Do you think you could help me with a few more of these?
Sure. Ask away.
Okay, next up, there's a math problem!
The answer is dance.
What's important is there was a song about it. It was pretty big back in the day... Maybe you're too young to know.
The answer is train riding.
Really? Are you sure about that?
I'm positive. It's fallen out of use these days, but that's what everyone used to call trains.
The answer is spinning.
Those spiders have some crazy organ in their abdomen that gives them the power to spin webs. Trust me, that has to be it.
Hmm... I don't know, that sounds wrong to me.
Well, I gave you my answer, and I'm sticking with it.
Wow, you seem pretty confident. Maybe you're right after all!
See, I've got the answers up here. All you need to do is ask.
Okay, next up there's a math problem!
(Of course there would be a math question. Hope I can figure it out.)

Question:
What is the probability of getting a total of 7 when rolling 2 dice?
The answer is 1 in 6.
Really? Are you sure? Let me see... To get 7 with 2 dice, that means a 1 and a 6, or a 2 and 5... Like that, right?
So there's 1 plus 6, 2 plus 5, 3 plus 4, 4 plus 3, 5 plus 2, and 6 plus 1. That's 6 possible combinations.
And for 2 dice, there are a total of 6 times 6, or 36 combinations. So a 6 in 36 chance makes it... 1 in 6!
You had it right! The correct answer <Italic>is</Italic> 1 in 6!
Just as I thought.
Wow, you seriously know your stuff! This is great! Who needs the answer book when I've got you? Okay, next up is a history question!
The answer is 7 in 36.
The answer is 1 in 2.
The answer is 1 in 3.
The answer is 5 in 12.
Really? Are you sure? Hmm... That doesn't quite seem to fit.
Hey, there are five possible answers, right? So I've got a 1 in 5 chance of being correct.
Well yeah, but what's that gotta do with it?
I've been up against worse odds than that before. Life or death situations, no less.
And yet I'm still here in one piece, aren't I? Don't you trust me to give you the right answer?
Hmm... That does make sense in a way. Your answer is probably right, then!
Then let's move on to the next question. Your exam is coming up soon.
Right! Okay, next up is Japanese history!
(Maybe in a past life I'd have known more about our history. Oh well, let's give this a shot.)
Question: Which United States Naval officer commanded ships in the War of 1812, and was instrumental in the "opening of Japan" to the West in the 1850s?
The answer is Commodore Perry.
Oh, you know what? That actually jogged my memory just now. I think you might be right!
Yeah. Before Commodore Perry came along, Japan was almost completely shut off to the rest of the world. It's hard to think that was only a century and a half ago...
You got that right. But enough thinking about the past! Next up, we've got physics!
The answer is Commodore Tokugawa.
The answer is Commodore Amigo.
The answer is Commodore Smith.
The answer is Commodore Johnson.
Hmm, I'm not sure you're right. I could have sworn it was Commodore Perry...
Hard to say for sure. It's not like either one of us was there to see it with our own eyes.
We all have to come up with our own answers for what happened back before we were born. And there's no room for doubt.
I'm not sure what that means, but it sounded pretty cool! Okay, I won't doubt you again!
We have to live in the moment and keep moving forward. So let's move on to the next question.
Okay, then! Next up is a physics question.
(Physics? This could be tricky.)
Question: What do you call the energy that an object possesses based on its mass and its height above the Earth's surface?
The answer is gravitational potential energy.
All right! That's what I was gonna guess!
Yeah, it seems to be the only one that makes sense. After all, science is a field of study that centers around discerning the facts from the lies.
Well said! You're certainly no liar yourself!
Okay, what's the next problem?
So this is the last one, and⑬wouldn't you know it⑬we're back at English!
The answer is electrical energy.
The answer is thermal energy.
The answer is kinetic energy.
The answer is magnetic energy.
Hmm. I don't understand how you reached that conclusion. How is this not gravitational potential energy?
Listen, I'm not one to go back on any answer I give. I'm sure the early pioneers in physics felt exactly the same.
They never let common sense hold them back. Instead they constantly questioned things, even if it caused them to end up as outcasts.
You may be right there. They do always say those famous physicists were way ahead of their time. But they always stuck to their guns!
Right. It all comes down to what you believe in. And studying is one of many ways to increase your capacity for learning, which in turn helps you choose what to believe.
Mm, I get you... In fact, I believe you! Man, I have a lot to learn.
Now, it's time for the last question. Ready for English round two?
(English again? Hopefully I'll get it right.)
Question: English often borrows phrases from Latin, a language from which it was heavily influenced. What does the Latin phrase <Italic>carpe diem</Italic> mean?
The answer is "seize the day."
Seize the day? ...Oh, yeah! I've heard that one before!
It's all coming back to me! That's the answer, all right!
The answer is "good idea."
The answer is "fish today."
The answer is "cheap carpet."
The answer is "underground parking."
I've got to admit, I have no idea what the answer is. They all look right to me.
"Carpe diem... carpe diem..."
The words may be unfamiliar, but by speaking them out loud, you get a sense of the meaning.
So... you just went with your gut?
Absolutely. That's why I have faith in my answer.
Wow... I've learned a lot from you today. I guess you really do need to be confident in your decisions.
I've never really been that mentally strong. That's why I always mess up in exams.
The more I think about a question, the less sure I get about the answer, so I just move on to the next one. That basically sums up my life.
Well, the right answer will always become clear eventually. When you're in the moment, you just have to believe in yourself and what you're doing.
You know what, you're totally right! Everything is much clearer now. I think I've got a chance at passing the practice exam today!
I think you're good to go. You look like a completely different person from before.
You think so? Thank you!
Sure. Are you good on time? The exam will be starting soon, won't it?
Oh, yeah! I'll let you know how it went after I take it. Can't thank you enough, sir!
Hey, guess what?
(Oh, it's that prep student from before. Looks like the exam is over.)
I finished the practice exam!
Uh-huh. And how do you feel about it?
It's strange... The exact same questions we were practicing came up again!
They did? Huh... What are the odds.
Yeah, so I aced the whole thing! I don't know how to thank you. I feel like I'm ready to take on the actual test now!
Really... Does that mean all the answers I gave you were right?
It sure does! Man, if it wasn't for you, I wouldn't have stood a chance.
But that's not all. I feel like today, you taught me something more important than what the right answers were. You taught me how to answer in general.
I did?
Yeah, it's like you said. "The right answer will always become clear eventually." That advice helped me stay calm and get through the rest of the test.
I get the feeling I'm a lot stronger mentally now. I think I'll do fine on the real exam... and in life!
That's good to hear. I'm glad I was able to help.
Um... This isn't much, but I'd like you to have it as a token of my thanks!
You got an <Color:8>Alertness Hood<Color:Default>.
